pages.text: Crash! "Let's play with everything!" Bami tipped the toy box with a foot. Wooden balls rolled, blocks scattered, and a little wooden train landed in the aisle. Playing was fun; tidying wasn't.
The train rattled over a river bridge. Balls rolled one way, blocks the other. On the way to the dining car for water, Bami stepped on a hard block. "Ouch!" Down onto their bottom!
Their favorite wooden train was missing, too. Bami checked quilts and beneath the bunk, but couldn't find it. Tears gathered. Nabi yawned from the window seat.
At a station, Dad came into the sleeping car. "Why so sad?" Looking at the aisle, he smiled. "Don't worry. I'll teach you some magic!"
Dad nudged a ball. "Leave things out, and every shake makes balls roll, blocks scatter, feet hurt, and the toy train hide!" Bami pulled their feet back. "An ouch-aisle!"
Dad tapped the empty box. "But tidy up, and feet feel fine, the toy train appears, and toys stay put when the train shakes! Back in place—that's box magic!" Bami wanted to try.
Dad taught a song. "One, same things together! Two, into the box! Three, close the lid!" Bami carried balls with their beak and stacked blocks with their feet. Balls and blocks back in place!
The last block went in. The aisle was clear and wide! Wings open, Bami strode along it. Nothing hurt their feet! Nabi waved a tail from the window.
Then Nabi yawned and shifted. Out from beneath the cat's tummy popped the little train! "My train!" Bami gripped it in a foot. "Tidying brings lost things back!"
Dad nuzzled Bami's head with his beak and hugged them. "Look how wide the aisle is!" After play, toys went back in the box and stayed there through every rattle. Back in place!
